review_status: Evidence reviewed 2026-11-17. CDFW/USGS/WDFW sources show white sturgeon is primarily riverine/estuarine and only occasionally marine; ocean SST and bathymetry factors are poor proxies for most life stages.

profile.size: Min limit 42 inches TL / Bag limit 1 per year / tag required
profile.diet: Small fish, crustaceans, squids, and pelagic prey
profile.behavior: Navigates West Coast kelp forests, rocky reefs, and coastal upwelling zones.

factors.reason_template: Water is {value} C, inside preferred Pacific temperature range for white sturgeon.
factors.value_notes: CDFW reports white sturgeon primarily in large rivers and associated estuaries, with only occasional ocean occurrence. CDFG/CA Marine Species Portal reports juvenile estuarine water temperatures around 15-20 °C in a Fraser River context, not marine satellite SST or adult thermal preference. The configured 8-18 °C / 10-16 °C SST band is not validated for the species' dominant river/estuary life history; keep values unchanged and mark needs_source.

factors.reason_template: Depth is {value} m, within prime Pacific depth zone for white sturgeon.
factors.value_notes: White sturgeon primarily occupy river channels and estuaries. USGS sampling found subadult/adult use of estuarine open-water shoals and deep channels averaging about 2-7 m; CDFW notes only occasional ocean excursions. The runtime bathymetry layer represents marine seafloor and does not capture river-channel depth or flow; the configured 2-30 m range is therefore a weak/poor proxy for most of the species' distribution.

text.day: Full daylight when Pacific gamefish actively hunt.

timing.note: West Coast captain reports and biological upwelling patterns.

regulations.summary: CDFW/WDFW: 42"-48" slot TL; strict tag limits
